Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

gentleman noun

also gentlemen, a real gentleman, gentlemanly, like a gentleman, a man of good family

classical

Ter. Ad. 464: neque bonī neque līberālis fūnctus officium est virī
Cic. Off. 2.64: līberāle

vir līberālis

phrase: līberālis, līberāle (adjective, third declension) with vir or homō

a gentleman: a man of a free man’s bearing, courteous and generous

Līberālis is “befitting a free man”: of conduct, noble, courteous, kind; of studies, the liberal arts; and very often “generous, open-handed” (Cic. Off. 2.56). In Plautus it can mean “handsome” (Lewis & Short). Līberāliter, like a gentleman (līberāliter ēducātus, Cic. Fin. 3.57).

Other words

  • ingenuus, ingenua, ingenuum — freeborn, of good birth; frank, worthy of a free man

    also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 65: apertē ōdisse magis ingenuī est (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    First “native”, then “freeborn” (as a noun, a freeborn man, against a freedman, lībertīnus), and so of character, noble, upright, candid (Lewis & Short).

  • vir honestus — a respectable man, a man of standing

    also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 281 (Lewis & Short, s.v. honestus)

    Honestus is “honoured, respectable”, and of conduct “honourable, decent” (Lewis & Short): a gentleman by standing rather than by manners.

  • vir bonus — a good and honest man

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.64 (Lewis & Short, s.v. bonus)

    A man of upright character, the Greek καλὸς κἀγαθός (Lewis & Short); in Cicero’s politics bonī are also the conservatives.

Examples

  • Quem frātrī adoptandum dedistī, neque bonī neque līberālis fūnctus officium est virī.

    The son you gave your brother to adopt has behaved neither as a good man nor as a gentleman should.Ter. Ad. 463–464

  • est enim nōn modo līberāle paulum nōn numquam dē suō jūre dēcēdere, sed interdum etiam frūctuōsum

    for to give up a little of one’s rights now and then is not only gentlemanly but sometimes even profitableCic. Off. 2.64

See also polite, man, kind.
